summary: Children in a column or a row with a gap from the spacing scale between them. Reach for it before writing flex CSS; `gap` takes the scale's steps and nothing else.
useWhen: laying out a group of things one after another — the sections of a page, the fields of a form, the controls of a filter row
a row of controls that should wrap onto more lines on a narrow screen rather than overflow

useInstead.when: the layout has columns that line up across rows — cards, stat tiles, a form in two columns
useInstead.why: a wrapping row lines its items up per line, not across lines; a grid keeps every row's columns the same width

useInstead.when: a row of related controls a keyboard user should cross with the arrow keys
useInstead.why: a Toolbar is one tab stop with arrow keys between its controls; a Stack is layout and leaves every control its own tab stop

useInstead.when: two or three actions at the end of a dialog, drawer or form
useInstead.why: it orders the primary action, and moves the rest into More actions when there is no room

composition.note: `direction` is `column` (the default) or `row`; `gap` is a step of the spacing scale — 16 by default. A row centres its children on the line and a column stretches them; `align` overrides either, `justify="between"` pushes the first and last to the ends, and `wrap` lets a row break onto more lines. Pass `as` for the element that means something — `ul` for a list (its bullets and indent are removed; give each child an `li`), `nav` for links, `form`, `fieldset`. Nest Stacks for a row inside a column; each keeps its own gap. Gaps by what they separate: 4 for tight pairs (an icon and its label), 8 for controls in a row, 16 for fields and items (the default), 24 for sections of a card or panel, 32 for sections of a page.

column.use: the default — things read top to bottom: page sections, fields, cards in a list

row.use: things along a line: a filter row, a name beside its avatar, suggestions; add `wrap` when it may not fit

children.note: laid out in order; `li` children when `as` is `ul` or `ol`

guarantees: layout only: it adds no role, so the element given by `as` — or the children — carry the meaning
the visual order is the DOM order: no `order` or reversed direction that would make reading and tabbing disagree
a row's children shrink to fit, so text wraps or is cut rather than pushing the row past the screen's edge
`as="ul"` stays a list to a screen reader while losing its bullets
requires: `as` for a group that means something — a list, navigation, a form — rather than a div
notes: It renders on a server. A gap off the spacing scale is a type error, not a style.

antiPatterns.dont: a hand-written `display: flex` with a pixel gap
antiPatterns.why: a gap outside the scale is the first place a screen drifts off the tokens, and nothing catches it

antiPatterns.dont: wrapping a single child in a Stack
antiPatterns.why: a gap between one thing and nothing is no layout at all — the Stack is noise in the tree

antiPatterns.dont: a Stack of cards that should line up in columns
antiPatterns.why: a wrapping row sizes each line on its own, so the columns never line up

antiPatterns.dont: reversing a row with CSS to put the primary action last
antiPatterns.why: the visual order and the tab order then disagree — write the children in the order they are read
